overview: Rako Hardeen is a bounty hunter identity (obi-wan kenobi) from Concordia (cover), documented across Clone Wars. Cover identity Obi-Wan used to infiltrate Moralo Eval's box tournament and foil kidnapping plot.
history:
Rako Hardeen rose from Concordia (cover) to become a bounty hunter identity (obi-wan kenobi) whose name appears on guild boards from the Core to the Outer Rim. Rako Hardeen was supposedly a deadly bounty hunter whose identity Obi-Wan Kenobi assumed via facial disguise to infiltrate Moralo Eval's box tournament and expose Count Dooku's kidnapping plot. Bounty puck archives, Imperial warrant logs, and Hutt contract registries all document Rako Hardeen as a contractor who shaped wars without wearing a uniform. Coverage spans all nine saga films, Clone Wars, Rebels, Mandalorian, Book of Boba Fett, Andor, KOTOR, KOTOR II, SWTOR, and Sith Empire-era mercenary markets.

Even before Rako Hardeen's career, Concordia (cover) produced hunters, soldiers, and syndicate enforcers whose traditions fed the modern guild system. Undercover Jedi hunter infiltration has precedent in Old Republic intelligence; Hardeen—real or fabricated—served as Clone Wars cover legend for Kenobi's Serenno operation. Old Republic bounty charters and Sith Empire mercenary rolls show how bounty hunter identity (obi-wan kenobi) contractors were hired to bypass political treaties. Mandalorian foundling laws and Hutt kajidic codes both influenced how hunters like Rako Hardeen negotiate payment and honor.

In the modern era, Rako Hardeen competed on postings issued by the Empire, the Rebellion, the Hutt Cartel, and independent monarchs alike. Obi-Wan's Rako Hardeen disguise fooled Cad Bane and Eval's box competitors, enabling Jedi to thwart Separatist assassin recruitment pipeline. Post-Endor guild restructuring and New Republic amnesty debates still reference contracts linked to Rako Hardeen. Mandalorian-era postings on Nevarro and Mos Espa show bounty hunter identity (obi-wan kenobi) specialists remain essential to galactic order—and chaos.

Rako Hardeen operated in war zones where capture alive paid more than kill, and both paid more than failure. Kenobi-as-Hardeen survived Eval's box trials on Serenno, earned Cad Bane's grudging respect, and prevented Moralo Eval from delivering kidnapped Chancellor Palpatine to Dooku. KOTOR-era Nar Shaddaa boards and TOR-era Great Galactic War contracts show earlier generations of bounty hunter identity (obi-wan kenobi) hunters in the same blood-stained market. Jedi, Sith, and clone troopers alike learned to respect or fear Rako Hardeen's approach to pursuit and extraction.
